{"narrative": "I opened a Wells Fargo Premier checking ( and linked savings ) account on XX/XX/year> at the XXXX XXXX XXXX Branch of Wells Fargo, where I was promised that with an offer code, if I bring in XXXX XXXX  into my new accounts by Day 45 and maintain it through Day 90, I will be paid XXXX XXXX. 

However, upon completing the activities, and not receiving my bonus, I contacted Wells Fargo to inquire about my bonus not posting. To my shock ( this was not told to me by the banker, who has since left Wells Fargo, and was a complete conman, in hindsight ), I was told that a " wire transfer '' does not qualify ( while the representative told me -- which sounded comical -- that I had to deposit money " in branch '' for it to count as a " deposit '' ) and that the system had deemed me ineligible to receive the bonus, and there was nothing they could do. 

I guess the shady conduct of Wells Fargo is not new to anyone who follows finance, and they continue their disgusting practices to this day. By inventing clauses to con customers, and not letting them know about it, they deliberately try to boost their " numbers '' while refusing to honor agreements ( unlike other reputable banks like XXXX XXXX XXXX ). 

I don't know what to say : is it expected that someone carry suitcases full of cash to the branch, to meet their " deposit '' requirement? Or do they expect me to have my employer pay me XXXX in salary in a day to " deposit '' to them? How in the name of XXXX does the most universally accepted form of depositing money -- a wire transfer -- not count? That too, without them telling me beforehand? 

How does Wells Fargo keep getting away with such disgusting, shady business practices; hiring conmen as " bankers '' to sell genuine-sounding lies to rake in business from customers? 

I kindly request CFPB to intervene, and get Wells Fargo to honor their part of the agreement, and pay me the XXXX XXXX  that they owe me."}
